review.headline: A lucky Pigeon lie framed the one honest Tit and won Blair the game.
review.summary: In Round 1, Blair was the only Meowfia. Blair invented a Pigeon visit to Ellis, and by chance it matched the egg Ellis really got from Alex the Turkey. The table eggsecuted Ellis, who had told the truth, and Blair banked 26 points alone. Farm caught the Meowfia in Rounds 2 and 3, Drew and then Alex, both times because that player was slow to claim a role. Blair's Round 1 haul held up, and Blair won 48 to Ellis's 44.

rounds.recap: Alex thought a Turkey gets an egg when visited, so he said Ellis's visit as the Tit was a lie. Ellis's real +1 came from Alex, but Blair's fake Pigeon claim explained it, so Ellis's story looked like the odd one out. Every other player threw at Ellis, a Farm player, and Blair won alone.

Casey the Eagle saw three visitors on Drew, and Finley's Owl report confirmed them, so all those claims checked out. Drew stayed quiet, then claimed Pigeon, which only the confused Blair could back up. Drew was eggsecuted as Meowfia. His fellow Meowfia Alex threw at him too and lost his cards.

Every player except Alex gave a role that seemed to check out. That included Casey the Mouser, who bluffed Falcon by echoing Blair's real Hawk visit. Alex dodged until the very end, then claimed Pigeon. Everyone else threw at him and he was eggsecuted as Meowfia.

highlights.text: Blair said they laid an egg on Ellis but really visited Casey, and the lie happened to match Ellis's real egg exactly.
Ellis said correctly that either Alex or Blair was lying, and the table ignored it and threw at Ellis.
Casey's Eagle list of visitors and Finley's Owl list of animals matched cleanly, which left Drew's story as the only one nobody could check.
Casey the Mouser bluffed Falcon and walked away clean. Alex, as Sphinx, should have known no Falcon was in play and never said so.

confusions.what: Thought a Turkey gains an egg when visited, so no egg meant no visitor. The Turkey actually lays eggs in the visitor's nest, so Ellis's claim was true.
Said only Finley's visit confused Casey, so Drew's visit to Casey looked odd. Any visitor confuses the Kookaburra, and Casey had three.
Blamed the confusion only on Finley's visit. Drew and Blair visited too.
Thought nests started the round at 4 and called Ellis's 6 cards and Alex's 3 suspicious. Players draw 2 on top of whatever they kept.
Accused Ellis over the same wrong nest math (6 cards but 'no eggs').
Used a Round 1 role report (Drew is Mouser) as evidence in Round 2, even though roles are re-dealt every round. Ellis did the same with his Tit guess.
His reasoning said he was testing Drew for Mouser, but he named Pigeon to the Tit.
Was Meowfia and noted that any Farm eggsecution would win it for him, then threw at Drew, his fellow Meowfia. He lost both cards.
Called Blair's nest of 3 odd when nothing changed. That is normal carry-over (1 kept + 2 drawn). Finley repeated it.
His reasoning said 'visit Alex' but he chose Casey.
As Sphinx he should have known the Farm roles in play, and there was no Falcon. He rated Casey 85% Meowfia but never challenged Casey's Falcon claim, and accused Finley instead.

review.title: The Lucky Pigeon Lie
problems: No one used a Wink, even though a Mouser was dealt in all 3 rounds. Players may not see what a mid-day kill is worth (removing a vote, silencing a claimer). The prompts may need to surface it more, or the card needs a clearer payoff.

Confusion is very costly. Casey (R1) and Blair (R2) both threw away real cards because of a false report. The Kookaburra was confused both times it was dealt, because popular targets draw several visitors. Consider not applying confused egg counts to the nest, or making the Kookaburra harder to confuse.
The Turkey learns nothing at dawn, and that led to the game's key misread. Telling the Turkey how many players visited would stop Round 1's wrong eggsecution.

Both Sphinx dawn reports showed only one player's role, not the full list of Farm roles the card promises. With the list, Casey's Falcon bluff in R3 could have been caught. Check whether the app is leaving that out.

Players misread nest sizes between rounds in every round after the first. Showing each nest's change since setup would cut the false leads. Also, one big win as the lone Meowfia in R1 (26 points) basically decided the game. Floofer and House Cat were never dealt.
